name: atlasfetch
description: Reverse geocode a coordinate to country, region, municipality and street, plus your own geofences.
long_description:
AtlasFetch answers **which place is this coordinate in?** A point becomes the country, region and municipality that contain it, with ISO 3166-1 and 3166-2 codes, plus matches from boundary sets you upload yourself: delivery zones, service areas, sales territories. Ask for the **street** layer and it also answers with the nearest street and, where one is mapped, the house number — worldwide.

**No sign-up needed to try it.** Leave the API key empty and it uses a shared public demo key, capped at 1,000 lookups a month across everyone using it. Get your own limits with a free sign-up at https://atlasfetch.xyz.

**Not for** forward geocoding or place search (an address to a coordinate), routing, distances, or downloading boundary geometry. House numbers are rare outside well-mapped areas.

Reference boundaries derive from OpenStreetMap under the ODbL. Coordinates you look up are not stored.

api_key.title: AtlasFetch API key
api_key.description: Optional. Create one free at https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard. Leave empty to use the shared demo key, capped at 1,000 lookups a month across all its users.

tools.name: lookup_location
tools.description: Resolve a coordinate to the country, region and municipality containing it, with ISO 3166 codes, optionally the nearest street and house number, and match it against your own boundary sets.

tools.name: list_boundary_sets
tools.description: List the boundary sets on your account, their boundary counts and which API keys may query them.

tools.name: create_boundary_set
tools.description: Create an empty set for your own polygons. Making it queryable is finished in the AtlasFetch dashboard.

tools.name: add_boundary
tools.description: Add one GeoJSON Polygon to an existing set on your account, with properties returned on every match. MultiPolygons are added part by part.
